title: Investigate a deploy health-check regression
raw_problem: After the latest API deploy, Kubernetes readiness checks fail for about 40% of pods. A teammate wants to roll forward with a larger timeout. Should we increase the timeout or isolate the deploy change first?
recommended_next_action: Compare the failing pod startup logs and config diff against the previous release, then run one canary with the suspected config reverted before changing readiness timeout globally.
open_questions: Which release diff changed startup, dependency initialization, or readiness behavior?
Do failing pods eventually become healthy, or do they fail on a specific dependency?
Would reverting the suspected config restore readiness without increasing timeout?
